title: Federal Judge Orders Release of Houston Shooting Witness; Cites Unconstitutional Detention
excerpt: U.S. District Judge Keith Ellison ordered ICE to release Jose Trinidad Rojas Pliego — a key witness to the Houston shooting who had been held without a bond hearing — finding his continued detention constituted an 'unconstitutional deprivation' of liberty.
content:
On July 27, 2026, U.S. District Judge Keith P. Ellison ordered the Department of Homeland Security to release Jose Trinidad Rojas Pliego, one of the passengers in the van when ICE agents fatally shot Lorenzo Salgado Araujo on July 7.

Judge Ellison wrote that Rojas Pliego had been held in ICE detention 'without an individualized bond determination' since the date of the shooting. 'Given the severity of this ongoing unconstitutional deprivation of Petitioner's liberty, the Court concludes that immediate release from custody is required,' Ellison wrote. DHS was required to release Rojas Pliego within 48 hours in a public space, return all personal identification documents, and give his attorneys at least three hours' advance notice.

  • Rojas Pliego and another passenger had both disputed the government's account of the shooting, asserting that ICE agents rammed Salgado Araujo's van before shooting him — directly contradicting DHS's self-defense claim.
  • Because the ICE agents at the scene had no body cameras or dashcams, Rojas Pliego and the other surviving passengers are among the only known witnesses to the shooting.
  • Judge Ellison noted that Rojas Pliego's habeas petition was 'one of hundreds of similar petitions' he had received regarding the Trump administration's detention practices.
  • The Harris County District Attorney's office had sponsored Rojas Pliego for a temporary victim witness visa to protect his ability to cooperate with the local criminal investigation.
